chunks: Is that (a tree in Paradise) a better welcome/hospitality, or the tree of Zaqqum?

key_terms.شَجَرَةُ الزَّقُّومِ: The tree of Zaqqum (a tree of bitterness in Hellfire)
key_terms.نُزُلًا: Hospitality or welcome (referring to the reward given to the righteous)

ai.seo_question: What is the tree of Zaqqum mentioned in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Surah As-Saffat, this verse employs a rhetorical contrast to highlight the ultimate fate of the disbelievers, specifically linking the 'tree of Zaqqum' to the Prophet Idris (AS) or the general class of the wicked depending on the tafsir. Shia scholars often interpret this as a vivid eschatological sign, where the Zaqqum serves not merely as a tree but as a manifestation of divine retribution for those who rejected the truth. The comparison underscores the tangible reality of the Hereafter, contrasting the 'better welcome' of Paradise with the bitter sustenance of Hell.
